record.paper_title: Research problem: The completion number of a graph
record.original_question: For a finite undirected graph G, the completion number of G is defined as the smallest integer k such that every partial positive Hermitian matrix whose graph is G has some Hermitian completion M with at most k negative eigenvalues, i.e. i_-(M) ≤ k. What graph-theoretic method or characterization determines the completion number of a given graph G? Equivalently, how can one characterize the class of graphs having completion number exactly k for each fixed k?

evidence.quote: Definition. Let G be an undirected graph. The completion number of G is the smallest number k such that every partial positive matrix A with graph G has a completion M with i−(M) ≤ k.

The following is our proposed Research Problem. Question: Given a graph G, how can one find its completion number? More specifically, it would be of interest to find graph theoretic characterizations of those graphs with given completion number.
We show that this number is not trivial, and we ask for a graph theoretic characterization of those graphs with a given completion number.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple undirected graph with vertex set V = {1,...,n}. A partial Hermitian matrix with graph G is a partially specified n×n array A = (a_{ij}) such that a_{ii} is specified for every i ∈ V, a_{ij} (and a_{ji} = conjugate of a_{ij}) is specified for every edge {i,j} ∈ E, and all other entries are unspecified. Such a partial matrix is called a partial positive (Hermitian) matrix if every fully specified principal submatrix (i.e. every principal submatrix indexed by a clique of G) is positive semidefinite.

A completion of A is any n×n Hermitian matrix M whose entries agree with the specified entries of A. For a Hermitian matrix M, let i_-(M) denote the number of its negative eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity).

Define the completion number c(G) of G to be the smallest nonnegative integer k with the following property: for every partial positive Hermitian matrix A with graph G, there exists a Hermitian completion M of A satisfying i_-(M) ≤ k.

Problem: Provide a graph-theoretic characterization that determines c(G) from G. Equivalently, for each fixed integer k ≥ 0, characterize the class of finite graphs G with c(G) = k.
artifact.status_search_result: The completion number was posed as a research problem and no graph-theoretic characterization appears in the literature. Related work (e.g. on inertias of band matrix completions) addresses special cases but not the general characterization. No subsequent publication appears to resolve it.

status_evidence.claim: Posed as an open research problem with no known general characterization.
